editorial:
The Phantom Empire is a 1935 Mascot Pictures serial directed by Otto Brower and B. Reeves Eason. Gene Autry plays a cowboy singer who runs a radio show from his Radio Ranch and finds the Muranians, an advanced civilization living beneath it, with television and ray guns. Frankie Darro and Betsy King Ross co-star. Its mix of western and science fiction, and its place as an early Autry vehicle, make it attractive to anyone who wants cheap, recognisable genre footage.

The rights trap is that the print's status is not settled. A 1935 film was published after the date that makes older films free by term alone, so its status depends on the 1962-63 renewal record. No renewal entry has been confirmed either way. The earlier check of the 1963 and 1964 catalog volumes did not record what was searched, and the 1962 volume and the Copyright Office catalog were not checked. The Internet Archive serial item shows a Public Domain Mark and the feature item shows a CC0 label, but both are the uploader's labels and prove nothing about copyright. Do not rely on them. Check the renewal sources yourself before reuse. Separately, the feature item (dated 1940 and also titled Radio Ranch) is a different edit built from the serial and needs its own check. The score and songs were not identified and are not cleared.
faq: Is The Phantom Empire safe to reuse?

Not yet confirmed. No renewal entry has been confirmed either way. The 1962, 1963 and 1964 renewal catalogs and the Copyright Office catalog still need a documented hand search before you rely on the print.
Do the Internet Archive's license labels clear the film?

No. The serial item shows a Public Domain Mark and the feature item shows CC0, but both labels are set by the uploader and are not evidence of copyright status. Rights depend on the renewal records for the 1935 film.
